newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Guangdong Power to report sharply higher 1996 net.
newsitem.headline: Guangdong Power to report sharply higher 1996 net.

text.p: Guangdong Electric Power Development Co Ltd will report a steep rise in its net profits for 1996 on expanded electricity output and its tax-exempt status, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.

The smooth operation of the firm's 51 percent-owned Zhanjiang Power Plant installed with two generators with a combined capacity of 600,000 kw boosted the company's output of electricity and profits, he told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
The firm's detailed 1996 results would be released to the public after being audited, the official said.
He said the company had obtained tax-exempt status for 1996 and this year, which also contributed greatly to its earnings growth.
Guangdong Power was granted the special tax treatment because it was classified as a foreign-funded company following its offer of class B stock to overseas investors.
In addition, the firm will pay 7.5 percent in corporate income tax annually during the 1998-2000 period. Most China-listed firms are assessed at a 15 percent tax rate.
At the end of 1996, the company had 213.25 million class B shares, accounting for 25.83 percent of its total share capital.
The firm said its interim net for 1996 surged 52 percent year-on-year to 293.14 million yuan over 192.83 million yuan, under Chinese accounting standards.
It said that under international accounting standards, it had net profits of 296.10 million yuan in the first half of 1996 versus the year earlier's level of 195.80 million yuan.
The firm reported after-tax profits of 371.03 million yuan for the whole of 1995, up only 0.19 percent over 370.29 million yuan in 1994, under Chinese accounting standards.
